newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean police say suspected N.Korean boat found.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean police say suspected N.Korean boat found.

text.p: A South Korean police official said a suspected North Korean ship with no engine was found on Tuesday near a beach where a Northern submarine ran aground last September.
The official, speaking by telephone from the eastern city of Kangnung, said a notebook containing a message of praise for Pyongyang leader Kim Jong-il was on the steel vessel.
It was not immediately clear whether the official was referring to a barge or to a ship with its engine removed.

The official, who declined to give his name, was contacted at a Kangnung police station. He said the vessel was spotted by a local resident at 10.50 a.m. (0150 GMT) on Tuesday. It was now being hauled ashore.
Yonhap Television News quoted unidentified officials as saying the black-hulled vessel might have drifted South during storms that lashed the east coast of the Korean peninsula.

The ease with which the submarine penetrated South Korea's coastal defences was a major embarrassment to the military and sparked public fears that the country was dropping its guard against possible Northern aggression.
